cards.context: Track 5 on Hail to the Thief (2003). The stuttering solo at the end is Greenwood's random Max/MSP patch, not a played part.
cards.headline: The guitar solo the computer plays by itself
cards.snippet: "Go to Sleep" closes with a guitar solo that no one quite plays. Jonny Greenwood built a patch in the music programming language Max that samples his guitar as he plays and plays the fragments back in randomized slices, muting his dry signal whenever a sample fires. The King of Gear, the reference site for Greenwood's equipment, describes it: "Once Jonny opens the Go To Sleep Max/MSP patch on his computer, it is always 'active'. Whether or not we hear its glitching, rather than Jonny's dry signal, is determined randomly by the patch itself. He just has a random generator running… All that Jonny does is hit his Boss LS-2 to incorporate the patch into his signal flow, then plays a lot of notes to ensure that the patch always has information to loop." He first used the patch on this song and "2 + 2 = 5"; it became so chased-after that in 2017 a pedal, the Feral Glitch, was Kickstarted at $260 specifically to recreate it.

cards.context: Hail to the Thief was released on 9 June 2003; "Go to Sleep" followed as its second single on 18 August, reaching No. 12 in the UK and No. 2 in Canada.
cards.headline: Leaked ten weeks early, and the title Yorke was begged not to use
cards.snippet: On 30 March 2003, ten weeks before release, an unfinished version of Hail to the Thief — rough edits and unmixed songs from January — leaked online. On Radiohead's forum, Jonny Greenwood wrote that the band were "pissed off," not with downloaders but because of the "sloppy" release of unfinished work; Colin Greenwood called the leak "like being photographed with one sock on when you get out of bed in the morning." The album's title plays on "Hail to the Chief": Yorke heard anti-Bush protesters chanting "hail to the thief," called hearing it a "formative moment," and chose it partly for Bush and partly in reference to the leak itself. (In 2025 he said Greenwood had "begged him" not to use it.) The songs' alternate titles came from Victorian music-hall playbills — this track's, "Little Man Being Erased," was briefly a candidate for the album title itself.

cards.context: From Hail to the Thief (Live Recordings 2003–2009), released in August 2025.
cards.headline: Live in London, 2003 — released 22 years later
cards.snippet: Radiohead's only London concerts in November 2003 were at Earls Court, and this performance sat unreleased for almost 22 years, surfacing in August 2025 on the band's official channel as part of the album Hail to the Thief (Live Recordings 2003–2009). Reviewing that album, Pitchfork heard this song "speed up and end in a glitching solo from Jonny" — Greenwood's random stutter patch at work on stage. The song was a staple of the 2003 tour, with 75 documented performances, but it has been played only twice since 2004, both times in 2012.

cards.context: Broadcast on Later… with Jools Holland on 27 May 2003; this upload dates from 2010.
cards.headline: The Jools Holland solo people remembered
cards.snippet: On 27 May 2003, weeks before Hail to the Thief came out, Radiohead played "Go to Sleep" on the BBC's Later… with Jools Holland, in a set with "There There," "2 + 2 = 5" and "Where I End and You Begin." Twelve years later, NME's readers voted it one of their favourite Later… performances; NME wrote that "it's Jonny Greenwood's guitar solo that makes the strongest impression," and one voter in the poll said: "Still remember Jonny Greenwoods awesome noise solo all these years after seeing it on TV."
